   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Steve Berry, PONTEFRACT

Dear Sir,

Do you know of anyone who whould
provide the service of convert-
ing commercial multi-load games
on tape that I own to run on +D
disc? FORMAT once published a
very technical article on this
subject but I'm afraid it went
straight over my head.

Thanks, and all the best.

          Steve Berry

Brian Cavers to Steve Berry

I know of no such service and I
doubt there is any simple way.
One would probably have to hack
through each individual game to
find the tape load routine and
replace it with calls to the +D
or Disciple ROM.

We have just received a "tape-to
-Plus D"utility from Danny Beach
which should appear in a future
issue. I have not had a chance
to study this yet but it seems
to transfer most files (even
without headers) from tape to
disc so it would partly help.
However, one would still need to
hack the game itself as describ-
ed above.

If I were to have a go I would
using something like SEEK'N PEEK
(OUTLET 45) or some other sector
editor to locate the directory
sector for the snapshot and find
where the register values are
stored (anyone already know?).If
you snapshot the game at the
moment it is waiting to load a
new level from tape then the
value of the program counter in
the code would reveal the place
where the load routine is!

It seems to me there's potential
here for an enthusiast and I'd
be happy to publish POKEs for
specific games (we have a snap
poker in this very issue!) Once
an enthusiast had cracked one or
two games it should get easier
for subsequent ones.

Whoever did it would also need
to know the right hook codes to
call in the Disciple/+D ROM to
load the new levels from disc.

A weak compromise is to snapshot
the game to disc, load each new
level from tape (the first time)
and snapshot it to disc.When you
next play you can just load and
play from the new level but of
course there's no continuity of
score, lives, ammo etc. It would
be alright for any games where
you just enter a code and start
at a higher level though or if
you just simply get tired of the
earlier levels and want to start
at a higher one.
                        - Brian

From: Simon Strange, WEST SUSSEX

What a brilliant edition OUTLET
No. 65 is. All the family enjoy
that well-known television
letters and numbers game so we
have been getting some practice
in on the number puzzle.

Then, towards the end, we find
TETRIS II, with all its various
challenging levels - I can't
think why I bought the original.
My son has managed to get to
Level 29 but now finds it a bit
boring having to make his way
through the same levels to pro-
gress any further. Would it be
possible to randomize the levels
so that they are in a different
order every time you play?


Alternatively, perhaps it would
be possible to introduce a pass-
word system so that the earlier
levels could be by-passed?

Finally, a big thank-you from my
10 year old son, Ben, for pub-
lishing his crossword and for
the cheque you sent which he has
put towards buying a new camera.
I suppose you haven't had a
chance to correct the bug which
gives the extra 'across clues'
when the last square of a line
and the first square of the sub-
sequent line are blank.

Once again, very many thanks for
all the OUTLETs. I wish you all
a very happy and successful New
Year.
                 - Simon Strange


Brian Cavers to Simon Strange

Crikey! You mean the mega-sized
crossword last month was created
by a 10-year old! Anyway, I can
see no easy solution to the
problem of the extra across clue
you found. Pity really because
I congratulated myself that in
all these years no bugs had been
discoved in what is quite a
complicated program! However,the
good news is that the extra clue
only appears in a crossword that
is 32 characters wide. This is
the reason why it has never been
spotted before - nobody has ever
created a maximum size crossword
before to my knowledge! I hope
Ben will be content to reduce to
a 31 by 31 crossword in future
which should solve the bug.

Last month's brilliant TETRIS
game was not written by us so we
have no idea how to make any
adjustments without a month's
work hacking into the code! Plus
D and Disciple users can just
snapshot their game position to
disc. You can do the same if you
buy a MULTIFACE 3 for `31.95
from ROMANTIC ROBOT UK LTD., 54
Deanscroft Avenue, london, NW9
8EN (TEL: 081 200 8870).It plugs
into the back of your Plus 3 and
when you have reached any point
or any level in virtually any
game you just press a button and
it is saved to disc. You can
later reload that and play from
that position. It also makes it
a lot easier to transfer games
from tape to disc.
                        - Brian

From: Ray Barnes, WESTBURY

The letter from D.J. Wood of
Cambridge has prompted me to
write to you yet again. Recent-
ly I have done 3 hardware jobs
including getting 'BRIGHT' back
on my 1084S monitor.

I'll start with this one. Ever
since I've had a monitor the
output from the +3 was connected
to the monitor TTL input, so, of
course, no'BRIGHT'as the +3 does
not have an intensity line.
Always at the back of my mind
was the thought that the +3
might have an analogue output
i.e. the strength of the actual
RGB signals vary in intensity
thus giving the bright effect.


So, getting the right monitor
plug from Mr. Tandy, I set about
connecting up the analogue in-
put. Two snags however, firstly,
the output from the +3 is far
too high to drive a standard
monitor analogue input. So I put
a 100 ohm resistor in series in
each of the R,G & B lines and
tidied these away inside the
monitor plug suitably wrapped in
insulating tape.

Secondly, the analogue input to
the monitor asks for separate
horizontal and vertical sync.
lines but the +3 only gives a
composite sync. Nothing ventured
nothing gained - I shorted the
two together in the monitor plug
and took the composite sync.
from the +3 to the junction.

Presto, it works perfectly. I
now have 'BRIGHT and spend hours
with 'Art Studio'making pretty
pictures.

Now, a +3 drive fault. One of my
+3's was failing to recognise
about 60% of discs and stopped
and asked for a tape LOAD, or
failing that would stop in mid
LOAD with the error report DRIVE
A NOT READY.After a small "teach
in" from Bob Brenchley of Format
on the general operation of disc
drives I concluded that the
discs were not reaching operat-
ing speed.

Stripping out the disc drive, I
checked the freedom of the disc
motor and the disc drive spin-
dle.

These seemed O.K. so I replaced
the drive belt with an elastic
band of about the same size.
About 6" long (total length),
3mm wide, and 1mm thick. To date
no more disc refusals or failed
LOADs.

If you're interested, here's how
to do it, but you do need a
steady hand and it's not for the
faint hearted...

With the Spectrum upside down,
remove 5 screws from the bottom.
Turn the Speccy over and remove
the 2 screws from the RH side.
Gently lift the keyboard from
the RH side and disconnect the
LED plug midway along the chass-
is.


Lean the keyboard against a
suitable pile of books on the
left. Remove the 2 screws secur-
ing the disc drive on the LH
side. Lift the drive from the
front and turn it over so it
lies behind the computer. Remove
the 2 plugs (gently) from the
rear of the drive. The drive is
now separate from the computer.
Unplug the 2 small plugs very
gently (one each side of the
drive). Lift the wire clip to
free the bundle of wires running
from the head to the PCB. Turn
the drive so the PCB is upper-
most. Very important from now
on; do not lift or turn the
drive otherwise the leafswitch
actuator is liable to drop out
and it's the very devil to get
back.

(I managed to drop it out and
went into a small panic). Remove
the 3 screws securing the PCB to
the drive and gently move the
board backwards away from the
drive slot for about 3mm to free
the indicator LED from its
housing.


You will now be able to raise
the PCB about 15mm and swing it
a short distance to the left.
You can now get to the drive
motor shaft, disc drive spindle
and belt. Check the tension of
the belt and the freedom of the
spindles. If you decide to re-
place the belt, lift it off with
a small screwdriver and put the
new one on in the same way.


Don't fall into the trap of try-
ing to make things easier by
taking other bits off the
drive, particularly the azimuth
sensor which is optically set,
and do make sure that your new
drive band doesn't have any
twists in it. Re-assemble in the
reverse order of dismantling.
You can check the drive runs OK
once you have connected the rear
plugs and before you put it back
in the Spec.


Finally, a printer fault. Mine
is a Brother 1109 but I think
it's probably common to many
printers. The ribbon drive did
not operate properly and new
ribbons would not drive at all.


The ribbon drive contains a
small spring wire clutch which
drives the ribbon one way as the
head is printing but slips as
the carriage is returning. If
you put a tight ribbon in the
printer one end of the wire
clutch can jump out of its loc-
ating hole (a sort of fail safe
mechanism).Then the ribbon drive
is at best intermittent, at
worst not at all.

Dismantle the clutch and reform
the wire drive and relocate it.
It's generally quite easy to get
to because it is just under the
case once it's removed. On
quotes received that little lot
above saved me nearly `200.

          Ray Barnes

Brian Cavers to Ray Barnes


Some great tips there Ray! Maybe
we should have a "GOLDEN PEANUT
OF THE MONTH AWARD" or something
for such good info!

                        - Brian

From: Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS

Perhaps someone out there can
shed some light on a very user
unfriendly bug that reared its
antennae whilst I was trying to
find some use for that wretched
VAL$ function. What I discovered
was that if you enter the foll-
owing lines and run them you get
the expected error message - but
note the line number!!

10 LET a$="hello" 20 PRINT VAL$
   a$
Now run the following:-

10 LET a$="hello"
20 PRINT : PRINT : PRINT VAL$ a$

That is even more unhelpful!!


My understanding of VAL$ is that
it expects to find at least 3
pairs of quotes for it to do its
job properly. But once again the
unexpected rears its head.

10 LET a$="123"
20 PRINT VAL$ "a$"

I even managed to do something
equally unhelpful using the VAL
function - but I forgot to note
it down so I cannot offer it
here. But since both functions
share much of the same ROM
routine, it's not really all
that surprising. Solution
anyone?

        Malcolm Goodman

From: K.A.Schimmel, NOTTINGHAM

Dear Whosoever will be reading
it,

A few OUTLETs ago there was a
program called 'ROTE' which had
been programmed in Danish (I
think)which became rather annoy-
ing in use. I LOADed it with
questions and answers from MAST-
TERMIND and,of course,the Danish
got in the way until one day I
LOADed the file accidentally
into Tasword 2 and found I could
erase all the offending lines
including the graphic flags then
reSAVE it and LOAD it back.

I was going to ask about Dr.Code
but Mr.P. Wheeler beat me to


it. However, I have gone back to
my Picturesque Assembler and
Monitor.

I kept my old rubber key model
when I upgraded to 128 and use
this when playing around with
M/C. I have also made a copy of
it on to +D disc but have, of
course, made do without print-
out and one can only SAVE the
code direct and not through the
assembler. Even so, the +D
should accept the Microdrive
syntax but doesn't in that case.
I wonder why?

There is another problem I have
with the +D transformer, I
think. Stuart Redfern and his
Dad's Card Index was just the
thing the Doctor ordered.

However, when I tried to format
for 40 cards it would only form-
at half the alphabet so I tried
for a less and a lesser number
of cards until I got down to 5
and at last got a full format
which, of course, was no good
for my purpose.

As it was time to pack in for
the day, I switched off and when
un-plugging the transformer I
found it was hot enough to al-
most burn my fingers. The next
morning I was going to write to
you for advice but thought I'd
try it once again. It formatted
all 40 without any trouble.

After a few hours transferring
data unto the cards I thought


I'd try again and the same thing
happened as the day before only
half the alphabet formatted and
a red hot transformer. Do you
think my transformer is on the
blink? Otherwise it seems to
work OK - it gets warm but not
over warm. What voltage is the
+D transformer?

I have written to Datel with SAE
but only got it back with a list
of phone numbers to ring.I wrote
again explaining that for health
reason (Tinnitus) which is made
worse by having to take up to 16
painkillers a day for sponduli-
tis and a form of sclerosis (NOT
MS)using a phone is not possible
as putting a receiver to my ears
is like standing on a station


platform while an express runs
through and trying to listen to
the station announcer, and, you
guessed,it I got another leaflet
of telephone numbers.

LONG LIVE OUTLET, AND ALL THE
BEST.

         K.A. Schimmel

Brian Cavers to K.A. Schimmel

Although you do type microdrive
syntax into the Picturesque
Assembler editor it does not use
the equivalent BASIC microdrive
syntax to actually do the loads
and saves but accesses the
Interface 1 direct from the
machine code which will not, of
course, be the same on a +D.

Your hot transformer CARD INDEX
problem seems wierd and might
just be coincidence.Try it a few
more times both cold and hot to
confirm as it might be something
you are typing in wrong. If it's
definitely re-occurring only if
the transformer is hot then it
does seem to be a hardware fault
you have.

It does seem unlikely that such
a hardware fault could cause the
particular problem you are
describing.Are no other programs
affected? If your Spectrum was
overheating then that might be a
different story as I suppose
some component might fail at
high temperatures and prevent
all the memory being accessed or
something.

If DATEL have sent you a list of
repair companies then you may
have to get someone to ring up
for you. However, I would most
definitely keep checking that
one program first as you would
probably be wasting your money
if it is a simple input error in
CARD INDEX.
                        - Brian

From: G.C. Wells, THETFORD

To Brian,

What about doing a program that
will SAVE and print a kind of
leaflet advertising the Chezron
Software that us members can
print out and do a few, or,
according to the reception we
get from the computer shops we
deal with, ask them if they
could possibly leave them where
old Specky users can see them.

Surely there are quite a lot of
ZX users that are not aware of
your existence especially if
they are as dumb as yours truly.
It would make an interesting
item for OUTLET and also, who


knows, keep you in the market,
after all, we all must know of a
shop that might want to get
people interested in buying up
what must be old stock of games
and other serious software.

Anyway, I am prepared to give it
a shot and it won't be a financ-
ial loss advertising that we old
Specky do still exist and that
the ZX is not buried. I am sure
quite a few members would rally
round.

What do you think?

            George
         (The old Git).

Brian Cavers to George Wells

Nice idea in theory but I can't
imagine any shop being willing
to have leaflets promoting goods
that are nothing to do with them
and for which they get nothing!
They would probably laugh at you
if you went in with a handful of
such leaflets and tell you to
clear off! I doubt they'd see us
as a means of encouraging people
to buy up their old stocks of
Spectrum games or utilities.

                        - Brian

From: Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS


Greetings Fellow Readers!


Please join me in an experiment
in mental telepathy...


Think of a number between 1 & 10

Multiply it by 9.

Take the digit(s) in your answer
and add them together to make a
single digit number.
      (e.g.,If your number
      was 78 then 7+8=15.)

From your number deduct 5.

Now using the relationship that
'1=a','2=b','3=c' and so on,con-
vert your number to its corres-
ponding letter of the alphabet.

Next, think of a country that
starts with that letter.

Now, take the second letter of
the name of that country and
think of an animal that starts
with that letter.

Finally, think hard about the
colour of that animal.

You are thinking of......

Please concentrate harder!
Yes I think I can sense it!
a....  Would it be a.....

  ...A grey Danish elephant?!!






              - Malcolm Goodman

From: Bjorn Nyberg, GLASGOW

It is always a great pleasure to
sit down and wallow through the
goodies of the latest issue so
I did today, when I received it.
Of course, I can't wait.

As you know, I have tried to
give advice - off the cuff - on
your business situation. Believe
me, if you think I can be of any
help in the future, just call
and we'll discuss.

I sat back today and tried to
think about today's computer/
games/consoles situation. If you
go back around ten years, it was
a console market.I remember see-
ing the Atari consoles with
cartridges.

Someone told me: "Don't bother,
get a home computer instead".

I didn't get anything until
early 1984, when I bought my
first Spectrum (48K). The
Spectrum was a sensation, I
thought. I originally bought it
to play games, then discovered,
however, very quickly, that it
offered much more.

Programming! This was the decid-
ing factor, I think: the friend-
liness of the Spectrum BASIC. (I
still prefer to program in 48K
mode on a 128K machine).


The fun of making the computer
obey your wishes.


Now, this is what serious people
like yourselves are about. To
encourage the home-based prog-
rammer to get into it, learn,
analyse, find out and create. To
demonstrate the fun and joy of
programming your computer.

I do not pretend to know half of
the techniques behind much that
you publish in OUTLET but at
least it is tantalising. When I
have time to get into machine
code seriously, maybe one of
these days...

Meanwhile, Spectrum BASIC is a
good enough vehicle for anybody.
Have you met any PC owner who
has written a program on his own
using any provided lanuage such
as GW BASIC?

I have not, though people to
whom I talk in business are sur-
prised that I can make up my own
spreadsheets!

When the Spectrum appeared, the
market was tired of the consoles
and responded to the value for
money approach of Sinclair
Research.

The magazines started to appear:
Sinclair User, ZX Computing,
Your Spectrum.All broadly orien-
ted but with the emphasis on
getting to know your Spectrum.
With interesting articles, tips
and reviews. You always felt you
were with it in this exciting
development period for home
computing.


Skilled game and utilities prog-
rammers also started to try out
the ultimate resources of the
humble Spectrum. With games abd
utilities that were affordable
by everybody, I daresay.

What a time we all had!

Planet of Death, Manic Miner,
Velnor's Lair, Jet Set Willy
(remember its success?), The
Hobbit, Tasword, Sabre Wulf, Dun
Darach, Lords of Midnight etc.
Those are some (very, very few
examples).


Then came the 16-bits after Sir
Clive sold to Amstrad. The Spec-
trum was finally discontinued.


So, except for the Spectrum, the
market is out of low-price prog-
rams. We may now be running the
full circle.


With the Spectrum ROM released
by Amstrad for use by other
machines(like the Russian Hobbit
and, perhaps, others), a ren-
aissance could come about -
maybe with some SAM technology
added. It will be interesting to
follow developments in the next
12 months. Maybe a two-tier
market with the 32-bits like the
new Amiga covering one half and
the Spectrum/SAM/Hobbit the
other. We shall see. I'd bet on
the programming factor, if only
it would get enough publicity.


Computers are there to do your
bidding - not only to run pre-
programmed utilities and games!

Best regards, and I wish you
both a very successful 1993. We
can all do with one I think.

         Bjorn Nyberg

From: F.G. Miles, WELWYN

I may be premature but I think I
have a solution to the SAVE @/
sector error problem.

It depends on the trial-and-
error conclusions that:

1) "Sector error" is produced
only by SAVE @, never by LOAD @

2) "Sector error" is produced
only when SAVE @ is commanded
with the disc stopped (but not
always even then): never when
it's already spinning.

If anyone has contrary experi-
ences I'd be glad to hear from
them.


If my conclusion is correct, the
remedy is fairly simple: when-
ever you want to SAVE @ on disc
drive d, first command LOAD @
d,0,1,0. This would LOAD track
0, sector 1 into ROM 0000 if the
ROM would accept it.It won't, so
the only effect is to spin the
disc: and I think, but haven't
yet used it often enough to be
100% sure, that once the disc is
spinning it won't make the sec-
tor error. The LOAD @ command
only takes a second or so. If
you do this you don't need to
double up the SAVE @ command:
this means a considerable speed-
ing up of some of my programs,
e.g. the IBU on this disc.

              - Francis G. Miles

Brian Cavers to Francis Miles

The trouble is, your LOAD @ 0
will crash on a Disciple because
the Disciple has its RAM at 0000
and its ROM at 8192 -the reverse
of the Plus D! There is no area
of memory that is always safe so
one needs to customise for the
particular program. Screen mem-
ory could be used if free or a
REM in the BASIC but I don't
recommend loading to 0000 except
in a Plus D-specific program.

Alternatively, does anyone know
of a short, simple test to show
whether a Disciple or Plus D is
attached? One could then use a
variable for the LOAD @ address.

                        - Brian.

From: Ray Barnes, WESTBURY

The letter from D.J. Wood of Cambridge has prompted me to write to you yet again. Recent- ly I have done 3 hardware jobs including getting 'BRIGHT' back on my 1084S monitor.

I'll start with this one. Ever since I've had a monitor the output from the +3 was connected to the monitor TTL input, so, of course, no'BRIGHT'as the +3 does not have an intensity line. Always at the back of my mind was the thought that the +3 might have an analogue output i.e. the strength of the actual RGB signals vary in intensity thus giving the bright effect.

So, getting the right monitor plug from Mr. Tandy, I set about connecting up the analogue in- put. Two snags however, firstly, the output from the +3 is far too high to drive a standard monitor analogue input. So I put a 100 ohm resistor in series in each of the R,G & B lines and tidied these away inside the monitor plug suitably wrapped in insulating tape.

Secondly, the analogue input to the monitor asks for separate horizontal and vertical sync. lines but the +3 only gives a composite sync. Nothing ventured nothing gained - I shorted the two together in the monitor plug and took the composite sync. from the +3 to the junction.

Presto, it works perfectly. I now have 'BRIGHT and spend hours with 'Art Studio'making pretty pictures.

Now, a +3 drive fault. One of my +3's was failing to recognise about 60% of discs and stopped and asked for a tape LOAD, or failing that would stop in mid LOAD with the error report DRIVE A NOT READY.After a small "teach in" from Bob Brenchley of Format on the general operation of disc drives I concluded that the discs were not reaching operat- ing speed.

Stripping out the disc drive, I checked the freedom of the disc motor and the disc drive spin- dle.

These seemed O.K. so I replaced the drive belt with an elastic band of about the same size. About 6" long (total length), 3mm wide, and 1mm thick. To date no more disc refusals or failed LOADs.

If you're interested, here's how to do it, but you do need a steady hand and it's not for the faint hearted...

With the Spectrum upside down, remove 5 screws from the bottom. Turn the Speccy over and remove the 2 screws from the RH side. Gently lift the keyboard from the RH side and disconnect the LED plug midway along the chass- is.

Lean the keyboard against a suitable pile of books on the left. Remove the 2 screws secur- ing the disc drive on the LH side. Lift the drive from the front and turn it over so it lies behind the computer. Remove the 2 plugs (gently) from the rear of the drive. The drive is now separate from the computer. Unplug the 2 small plugs very gently (one each side of the drive). Lift the wire clip to free the bundle of wires running from the head to the PCB. Turn the drive so the PCB is upper- most. Very important from now on; do not lift or turn the drive otherwise the leafswitch actuator is liable to drop out and it's the very devil to get back.

(I managed to drop it out and went into a small panic). Remove the 3 screws securing the PCB to the drive and gently move the board backwards away from the drive slot for about 3mm to free the indicator LED from its housing.

You will now be able to raise the PCB about 15mm and swing it a short distance to the left. You can now get to the drive motor shaft, disc drive spindle and belt. Check the tension of the belt and the freedom of the spindles. If you decide to re- place the belt, lift it off with a small screwdriver and put the new one on in the same way.

Don't fall into the trap of try- ing to make things easier by taking other bits off the drive, particularly the azimuth sensor which is optically set, and do make sure that your new drive band doesn't have any twists in it. Re-assemble in the reverse order of dismantling. You can check the drive runs OK once you have connected the rear plugs and before you put it back in the Spec.

Finally, a printer fault. Mine is a Brother 1109 but I think it's probably common to many printers. The ribbon drive did not operate properly and new ribbons would not drive at all.

The ribbon drive contains a small spring wire clutch which drives the ribbon one way as the head is printing but slips as the carriage is returning. If you put a tight ribbon in the printer one end of the wire clutch can jump out of its loc- ating hole (a sort of fail safe mechanism).Then the ribbon drive is at best intermittent, at worst not at all.

Dismantle the clutch and reform the wire drive and relocate it. It's generally quite easy to get to because it is just under the case once it's removed. On quotes received that little lot above saved me nearly `200.

Ray Barnes

Теперь о неисправности дисковода +3. Один из моих +3 отказывался распознавать около 60% дисков: останавливался и просил загрузку с ленты (tape LOAD) или же прерывал чтение на полпути с ошибкой DRIVE A NOT READY. После небольшого ликбеза от Bob Brenchley из журнала Format по поводу общих принципов работы дисководов я пришел к выводу, что диски не набирают рабочую скорость.

Разобрав дисковод, я проверил плавность хода двигателя и шпинделя привода диска.

С ними все было в порядке, поэтому я заменил пассик обычной канцелярской резинкой примерно такого же размера: около 6 дюймов в длину (общая длина окружности), 3 мм шириной и 1 мм толщиной. На сегодняшний день — ни одного сбоя диска или неудачной загрузки.

Если кому интересно, вот как это сделать, но вам понадобится твердая рука, и это занятие не для слабонервных...

Положив Spectrum дном кверху, выкрутите 5 винтов снизу. Переверните Speccy и выкрутите 2 винта с правой стороны. Осторожно приподнимите клавиатуру справа и отключите разъем светодиода посередине шасси.

Обоприте клавиатуру на подходящую стопку книг слева. Выкрутите 2 винта, крепящих дисковод с левой стороны. Приподнимите привод спереди и переверните его так, чтобы он лег позади компьютера. Аккуратно снимите 2 разъема с задней части дисковода. Теперь дисковод отделен от компьютера. Очень аккуратно отключите 2 небольших разъема (по одному с каждой стороны привода). Приподнимите проволочный зажим, чтобы освободить жгут проводов, идущий от головки к плате. Поверните дисковод платой вверх. Очень важный момент: с этого момента не поднимайте и не переворачивайте привод, иначе толкатель лепесткового микропереключателя может выпасть, а вернуть его на место — сущий ад.

(У меня он вывалился, и я слегка запаниковал). Выкрутите 3 винта, крепящих плату к дисководу, и аккуратно сдвиньте плату назад, в сторону от щели дисковода, примерно на 3 мм, чтобы освободить светодиодный индикатор из его гнезда.

Теперь вы сможете приподнять плату примерно на 15 мм и немного сдвинуть ее влево. Теперь открыт доступ к валу двигателя привода, шпинделю и пассику. Проверьте натяжение пассика и легкость вращения шпинделей. Если решите заменить пассик, снимите его с помощью маленькой отвертки и точно так же наденьте новый.

Не попадитесь в ловушку, пытаясь облегчить себе задачу снятием других деталей дисковода, особенно датчика азимута, который юстируется оптически, и обязательно убедитесь, что новый пассик нигде не перекручен. Сборка производится в обратном порядке. Вы можете проверить работу дисковода, как только подключите задние разъемы, еще до установки его обратно в корпус Spectrum.

И наконец, неисправность принтера. У меня Brother 1109, но, думаю, эта проблема характерна для многих принтеров. Механизм протяжки красящей ленты работал неправильно, а новые картриджи вообще не крутились.

Привод ленты содержит небольшую проволочную пружинную муфту, которая протягивает ленту в одну сторону во время печати головки, но проскальзывает при возврате каретки. Если вставить в принтер тугую ленту, один из концов проволочной муфты может выскочить из посадочного отверстия (своего рода механизм защиты). После этого подача ленты работает в лучшем случае с перебоями, в худшем — не работает вовсе.

Разберите муфту, подогните проволочный поводок и установите его на место. Добраться туда обычно довольно легко, так как он находится прямо под корпусом, стоит его только снять. Судя по расценкам в мастерских, все вышеперечисленное сэкономило мне почти £200.
